title: Channels, Carriers and Pumps
short: Ions and polar molecules cross through proteins. Facilitated diffusion goes down the gradient with no energy; active transport, like the sodium-potassium pump, uses ATP to move against it.
trouble: Students think any transport that uses a protein must use energy. Channels and carriers in facilitated diffusion use none; only moving against the gradient costs ATP.

blocks.html: Ions and polar molecules cannot slip through the oily middle of the membrane. They cross through proteins. The question that sorts every case is simple: are they going down their gradient or up it?

Facilitated diffusion moves substances down their gradient through channel or carrier proteins, with no energy from the cell. Active transport uses energy, usually ATP, to move substances against their gradient. The sodium-potassium pump is the classic example.

head: Kind
Direction, protein, energy
Examples
rows: Down the gradient; no protein; no energy
Down the gradient; a channel or carrier; no energy
Against the gradient; a pump; uses ATP
The sodium-potassium pump; roots taking up minerals
blocks.cap: Passive transport (the first two) versus active transport.

blocks.name: bi-membrane
blocks.cap: Facilitated diffusion: particles pass through a channel, from crowded to less crowded.

blocks.name: bi-membrane
blocks.cap: Active transport: a pump spends ATP to move particles to the crowded side.

blocks.html: Going down a gradient happens on its own, like rolling downhill; a channel or carrier just gives the particle a path. Going up a gradient is like pushing a cart uphill: it needs a power source. The sodium-potassium pump uses one ATP to move 3 Na⁺ out of the cell and 2 K⁺ in, both against their gradients. The gradients it builds are stored energy: nerve cells use them to send signals, and many cells use the sodium gradient to pull glucose in.

blocks.title: Passive or active?
blocks.q: Root cells hold many times more potassium than the soil water around them, yet they keep taking more in. Passive or active?
steps: Potassium moves from the soil (low) into the cell (high).
Moving against a gradient needs energy: active transport.

blocks.title: Pump arithmetic
blocks.q: A cell's sodium-potassium pumps use 400 ATP. How many Na⁺ and K⁺ ions do they move?
steps: Each ATP moves 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in.

blocks.html: Thinking any transport that uses a protein must use energy. Channels and carriers in facilitated diffusion use none: the gradient drives the movement. Only moving against the gradient costs ATP. Sort by direction first, not by whether a protein is involved.
